A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Deep Edge Filter study, with readable text, equations, tables, figures and complete Appendices A-F. Corresponding content can be matched despite layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original linear-probing, vision, language, NeRF and audio experiments, together with appendix results on cross-domain classification and a convolution-layer control.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark comparisons and supplementary experiments in Appendices B-F.

M1.justification: The high-pass operation h minus LPF(h), architecture-specific 1D/2D filtering, reflect padding, detached LPF branch and single-layer insertion remain unchanged in Section 3.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CIFAR/ImageNet corruption benchmarks, GLUE tasks, Blender scenes, UrbanSound8K and PACS/DomainNet transfer scenarios. CIFAR naming edits do not change coverage; the foundation-model experiments already appear in v1 Appendix E.

E2.justification: The evaluated vanilla models, NORM/TENT methods, alternative filters and convolution-layer control are retained. Table 2 adds ResNet18 to its backbone label, but v1 Appendix A.1 already identifies ResNet18 for the same ImageNet200 evaluation.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model assignments, corruption severity, filter configurations, metrics and evaluation procedures remain unchanged, including Appendices A and E-F. Matching Table 2 to Appendix A.1 establishes that its backbone-label correction does not introduce a different experimental setting.

E4.justification: The filter-type, position and kernel-size ablations, activation-density/FFT analyses, NeRF examples, t-SNE visualizations and computation-matched convolution control are retained. Relocating their displays adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both Appendix B sections report five independent baseline runs with different random seeds, means and standard deviations in Table 6, and gains normalized by baseline standard deviation in Figure 5. Only Figure 5's placement changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1-10 and the plotted and prose findings are unchanged. For example, both report SST-2 baseline/filter accuracies of 79.36/80.85 and audio accuracies of 77.42/81.72. Added dashes for unavailable ViT NORM evaluations in Table 2 introduce no experimental outcomes.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(4), the semantic/domain feature decomposition, frequency assumptions and sparse-coding argument are unchanged. No mathematical definition, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about modality-independent deep-feature filtering, improved generalization and the separation of semantic from domain-specific information.

C2.justification: Mechanism interpretations and qualifications remain unchanged, including explanations for the ficus degradation and Gaussian-filter results on ViT. The conclusion retains the same computational-cost, model-scale and language-model limitations.

D1.justification: Table 2 corrects its CNN backbone label from WRN28-10 to WRN28-10/ResNet18, making architecture reporting consistent with the existing Appendix A.1. This is a limited documentation correction; implementation settings, hardware information and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 53 references are retained. Positioning relative to frequency-based methods, activation filtering and sparsity research is unchanged.

P1.justification: Local terminology edits standardize several CIFAR names, specify CIFAR-100 in the linear-probing discussion and replace Domain with Modality in Table 5. The prose, section sequence and overall narrative remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 moves from page 5 to page 6 and receives corrected labels and missing-value markers. On page 7, the NeRF discussion now precedes Table 4 and Figure 2; Appendix Figure 5 moves above its explanatory paragraph. The displays retain their underlying content and designs.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly improves reporting clarity by correcting Table 2's backbone identification to agree with Appendix A.1 and explicitly marking unavailable ViT NORM entries. Terminology cleanup also reduces ambiguity. The scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged, so these corrections support a limited overall improvement.
